title.title: The Mahler conjectures in every dimension
title.subtitle: Claim: $|K|\,|K^\circ| \ge 4^n/n!$ for symmetric bodies, and the simplex floor for all bodies, in every $\mathbb{R}^n$

plain: Pair a shape with its 'dual' and multiply their volumes: which shape makes that product smallest?

object.heading: In the plane: a body $K$ and its polar $K^\circ$, along the $\ell_p$ balls

beats.text: The disc is its own polar, and there the volume product $|K|\,|K^\circ|$ is largest
Push $K$ to the square: $K^\circ$ becomes the diamond, and the product falls to $4^n/n!$
Mahler (1939): no symmetric body goes lower. Proved before only for $n \le 3$

steps: Put the body in position space and its dual in momentum space
Fit a round symplectic ball of capacity close to four inside
Symplectic maps keep volume, so the product beats the ball's

achievement.label: Mahler's conjectures (1939), symmetric and general
achievement.context: Before: dimensions 2 and 3 only, special classes, and Bourgain–Milman's $c^n/n!$

verify.detail: Four Comparator statements: both inequalities, both equality cases, and Gromov width 4
verify.ourCheck: We read the symmetric statement for traps; we did not build the Lean

voice.text: A shape and its dual. Push the disk to a square; the volume product falls.
Fit a round ball inside the body times its dual; volume does the rest.
Claimed: no symmetric body goes lower.

sources.quote: for every origin-symmetric convex body K in R^n, n>=1, |K||K°| >= 4^n/n!, with equality iff K is a linear image of a Hanner polytope
min_z |K||(K-z)°| (Santaló point) >= (n+1)^{n+1}/(n!)^2, equality iff K is a simplex
Blaschke and Santaló showed its maximum is the Euclidean ball's.
Before this release the conjecture was settled in dimensions two and three only.
Four Comparator challenges cover the symmetric inequality, its equality classification, the general inequality with its simplex equality case, and the Gromov width.
I read it for traps and found none.
Not formalized: functional Mahler inequalities and entropy-transport corollaries; embedding at capacity exactly 4.
